content.title: About
content.content: Pepperoni pizza is an Italian‑style dish popular in restaurants and fast‑food outlets. A thin or crispy crust (type 3399) is topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and slices of spicy cured sausage called pepperoni.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “pepperoni” comes from the Italian “peperone,” meaning sweet pepper, though in the U.S. it refers to a spicy pork‑beef sausage.
Pepperoni pizza became one of the best‑selling pizza varieties in the United States during the 1970s.
Traditional pizza is baked in a wood‑fired oven at 400–500 °C, giving the crust a distinctive aroma and crunch.
A “double pepperoni” version doubles the meat layer for an extra‑intense flavor.
Some regions drizzle honey or barbecue sauce on the pizza for a sweet‑spicy contrast.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pepperoni and mozzarella provide a substantial amount of protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Pepperoni contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 from the meat supports nerve function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella is a good source of calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pepperoni and prepared sauces often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Processed meats and cheese contain saturated fats that, in excess, may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk proteins should avoid traditional mozzarella‑topped pizza.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate
items.content: Some sauces use MSG, which can cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pepperoni pizza is usually served hot, sliced into wedges. Fresh basil, a drizzle of olive oil, or extra spices can be added to taste. For extra crunch, the crust can be briefly reheated in an oven or grill.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.
